'''Barbara Jean Francis Apgar''' (born March 4, 1936) is an American biochemist. She worked on important research on [[RNA|ribonucleic acids]] (RNA), and on [[zinc deficiency]] as a risk factor in reproduction. She won the [[Federal Woman's Award]] in 1970, and the [[Arthur S. Flemming Award]] in 1973.

== Early life and education ==
Barbara Jean Francis was born in [[Tyler, Texas]], the daughter of Albert Edward Francis and Mary Agnes Linehan Francis.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1970-03-13|title=Native Texan Youngest U.S. Woman Honored|pages=16|work=The Baytown Sun|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87877326/native-texan-youngest-us-woman-honored/|access-date=2021-10-27|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Her father was a railroad engineer.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1985-06-24|title=A. E. 'Bert' Francis Services Tuesday|pages=8|work=The Tyler Courier-Times|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87877529/a-e-bert-francis-services-tuesday/|access-date=2021-10-27|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She completed undergraduate studies in chemistry at [[Texas Woman's University]], and earned her master's degree and Ph.D. at [[Cornell University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|date=1970-02-16|title=Woman Honored for Federal Service; Youngest to Get Award|pages=13|work=The Ithaca Journal|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87876902/woman-honored-for-federal-service/|access-date=2021-10-27|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Her 1959 master's thesis was titled "The effect of conventional and electronic cooking on the [[thiamine]] content of pork patties, roasts, and chops";<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=The effect of conventional and electronic cooking on the thiamine content of pork patties, roasts, and chops.|date=1959|place=Ithaca, N.Y.|language=English|first=Barbara Jean Francis|last=Apgar| oclc=63363988 }}</ref> her 1964 doctoral dissertation was titled ''Separation of [[Escherichia coli|E. coli]] [[leucine]]-acceptor RNAs''.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Apgar|first=Barbara Jean Francis|url=http://catalog.hathitrust.org/api/volumes/oclc/63340975.html|title=Separation of E. coli leucine-acceptor RNAs.|date=1964|location=Ithaca, N.Y.|language=English|oclc=693121271}}</ref>

== Career ==
Apgar worked for the [[United States Department of Agriculture]] (USDA) as a biochemist in the Plant, Soil and Nutrition Laboratory at Cornell University. She was a member of a team studying the structure of ribonucleic acids (RNA) with [[Robert W. Holley]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Holley|first1=Robert W.|last2=Apgar|first2=Jean|last3=Everett|first3=George A.|last4=Madison|first4=James T.|last5=Marquisee|first5=Mark|last6=Merrill|first6=Susan H.|last7=Penswick|first7=John Robert|last8=Zamir|first8=Ada|date=1965|title=Structure of a Ribonucleic Acid|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1715055|journal=Science|volume=147|issue=3664|pages=1462–1465|doi=10.1126/science.147.3664.1462|jstor=1715055|pmid=14263761|bibcode=1965Sci...147.1462H |s2cid=40989800|issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The team won a 1965 USDA Distinguished Service Award, and Holley received a [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine|Nobel Prize]] in 1968, for that work.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Robert W. Holley Biography|url=https://www.ars.usda.gov/northeast-area/ithaca-ny/robert-w-holley-center-for-agriculture-health/docs/robert-w-holley-biography/|access-date=2021-10-27|website=USDA ARS}}</ref> "Being the first person to do something has a certain fascination," she later wrote, "but it isn't an experience most of us expect to have."<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Apgar|first=B. Jean|date=1968|title=Mountain Climbing in a Laboratory|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=H9EQw3HB0uMC&dq=Jean+Apgar+Agriculture&pg=PA307|journal=Yearbook of Agriculture|pages=307–310}}</ref> Her research in the 1970s focused on the role of [[zinc]] in reproductive physiology, and on zinc deficiency as a maternal and fetal health risk during pregnancy and delivery.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|date=1973-03-01|title=Scientist Jean Apgar Wins Another Honor|pages=23|work=The Ithaca Journal|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87875845/scientist-jean-apgar-wins-another-honor/|access-date=2021-10-27|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

In 1970, she was one of the six recipients of the Federal Woman's Award,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Jones|first=Dorothy B.|date=April–June 1970|title=The Tenth Annual Federal Woman's Award|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7FGN-D95fX0C&dq=Jean+Apgar+Agriculture&pg=RA3-PA25|journal=Civil Service Journal|volume=10|pages=25}}</ref> and the youngest woman to receive that honor.<ref name=":0" /> In 1972, she received an Arthur S. Flemming Award, given annually to ten promising young employees of the federal government.<ref name=":2" />

== Selected publications ==
Between 1959 and 1997, Apgar published dozens of research articles in academic journals including ''[[Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics|Journal of the American Dietetic Association]]'',<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Apgar|first1=Jean|last2=Cox|first2=Nancy|last3=Downey|first3=Irene|last4=Fenton|first4=Faith|date=1959-12-01|title=Cooking Pork Electronically1. Effect on Cooking Time, Losses, and Quality|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0002822321179544|journal=Journal of the American Dietetic Association|language=en|volume=35|issue=12|pages=1260–1269|doi=10.1016/S0002-8223(21)17954-4|s2cid=239492499|issn=0002-8223|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]'',<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ja01484a040|doi=10.1021/ja01484a040|title=Nucleotide and Oligonucleotide Compositions of the Alanine-, Valine-, and Tyrosine-Acceptor "Soluble" Ribonucleic Acids of Yeast|year=1961|last1=Holley|first1=Robert W.|last2=Apgar|first2=Jean|last3=Merrill|first3=Susan H.|last4=Zubkoff|first4=Paul L.|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=83|issue=23|pages=4861–4862|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''[[Journal of Biological Chemistry]],''<ref name=":5">Apgar, J., Holley, R. W., & Merrill, S. H. (1962). [https://www.jbc.org/article/S0021-9258(18)60374-6/pdf "Purification of the alanine-, valine-, histidine-, and tyrosine-acceptor ribonucleic acids from yeast"] ''Journal of Biological Chemistry'', ''237''(3), 796-802.</ref> ''[[American Journal of Physiology]],''<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal|last=Apgar|first=J|date=1968-07-01|title=Effect of zinc deficiency on parturition in the rat|url=https://journals.physiology.org/doi/abs/10.1152/ajplegacy.1968.215.1.160|journal=American Journal of Physiology. Legacy Content|volume=215|issue=1|pages=160–163|doi=10.1152/ajplegacy.1968.215.1.160|pmid=5659329|issn=0002-9513|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''[[Journal of Nutritional Biochemistry]]'',<ref name=":7">{{Cite journal|last=Apgar|first=Jean|date=1992-06-01|title=Zinc and reproduction: an update|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0955-2863%2892%2990032-E|journal=The Journal of Nutritional Biochemistry|language=en|volume=3|issue=6|pages=266–278|doi=10.1016/0955-2863(92)90032-E|issn=0955-2863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''[[Journal of Animal Science]]'',<ref name=":8">{{Cite journal|last1=Apgar|first1=Jean|last2=Fitzgerald|first2=James A.|date=1985-06-01|title=Effect on the Ewe and Lamb of Low Zinc Intake throughout Pregnancy|url=https://doi.org/10.2527/jas1985.6061530x|journal=Journal of Animal Science|volume=60|issue=6|pages=1530–1538|doi=10.2527/jas1985.6061530x|pmid=4019343|issn=0021-8812|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and ''[[Journal of Nutrition]]''.<ref name=":9">{{Cite journal|last=Apgar|first=Jean|date=1970-04-01|title=Effect of Zinc Deficiency on Maintenance of Pregnancy in the Rat|journal=The Journal of Nutrition|volume=100|issue=4|pages=470–476|doi=10.1093/jn/100.4.470|pmid=5439355|issn=0022-3166|doi-access=free}}</ref> Some of her articles include the following:

== Personal life ==
Jean Francis married Ronald W. Apgar in 1958; they lived in [[Ithaca, New York]], and had three children.<ref name=":2" /> "The children went to the laboratory with me," she explained, adding "I have very efficient children."<ref name=":0" /> Her son Michael died in a car accident in 1985.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1985-10-21|title=Obituary for Michael A. Apgar (Aged 25)|pages=5|work=The Ithaca Journal|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87882697/obituary-for-michael-a-apgar-aged-25/|access-date=2021-10-28|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>
